reason: The myoblasts must fuse to form the multinucleated muscle fibres described in the introduction.
expectation: The fusion proteins will join the myoblasts into a multinucleated muscle cell.

effect: The myoblasts fused and matured into a fibre with sliding filaments; its actin grip sites are still covered.
reaction: The distinction between one long fibre and its many nuclei is useful.
reason: The calcium pulse is the visible signal likely to enable the filament machinery to pull.
expectation: Calcium will uncover actin’s grip sites and allow the fibre to contract.

effect: Calcium enabled filament sliding and produced a shortening fibre; it now needs to return to its ready state.
reaction: The distinction between shortening the fibre and shortening the filaments is useful.
reason: The calcium-pumping membranes should remove the calcium signal and prepare the fibre to relax.
expectation: ATP-powered pumps will return calcium to storage, allowing the fibre to relax and become ready again.

effect: Calcium pumping stopped the pull and completed the fibre’s contraction-and-reset goal; the muscles and attachments remain.
reaction: It is useful that relaxation also requires ATP and that an outside pull lengthens the fibre.
reason: The empty biceps sheaths appear ready to receive muscle fibres.
expectation: The fibre will help fill the biceps sheaths to form a muscle with tendons.

effect: The fibre first needed collagen-rich connective layers to form fascicles; enough bundles remain for both muscles.
reaction: The intermediate bundling step was unexpected but clarifies the tissue organization.
reason: The fascicles can now plausibly fill the empty biceps sheaths and connect to their tendons.
expectation: The fascicles will form the biceps muscle within its sheaths and tendons.

effect: The fascicles formed the two biceps heads, with connective tissue carrying force to their tendons.
reaction: The force pathway from fibres to tendon is a useful connection.
reason: The remaining fascicles should also fill the three triceps head spaces.
expectation: The fascicles will form the triceps within its sheaths and tendons.

effect: The remaining fascicles formed the three triceps heads, leaving both muscles ready for attachment.
reaction: The different origins and joint crossings of the triceps heads are informative.
reason: The biceps tendons are shown extending toward the shoulder and radius, so the movable skeleton is the natural next attachment.
expectation: The biceps tendons will attach to the arm skeleton across the elbow.
